items.title: Constructible subsets of a scheme
items.statement: A subset Z of a topological space X is constructible if it is a finite union of intersections U minus V of retrocompact opens U,V; an open is retrocompact when its intersection with every quasi-compact open is quasi-compact. For X=Spec A the retrocompact opens are exactly the quasi-compact opens, so constructible sets are the finite unions of D(f)∩V(g_1,…,g_m). The empty union is allowed.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Topology, Section 5.15 (tags 0059, 04ZC) and Morphisms of Schemes, Section 29.23
The Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, Section 10.29

items.title: Flat morphism of schemes
items.statement: A morphism f:X→S is flat at x if the local ring map O_{S,f(x)}→O_{X,x} makes O_{X,x} flat as an O_{S,f(x)}-module; f is flat if this holds for every x. The empty source is flat vacuously.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.title: Affine-local flatness
items.statement: For affine charts U=Spec B⊂X and V=Spec A⊂S with f(U)⊂V, f is flat at x∈U iff B_q is flat over A_p, where q represents x and p=q∩A. It is flat on U iff B is flat over A; these tests agree on refining affine covers.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Identify stalks with localizations. A flat B stays flat after localizing B at q and then A at p. Conversely localize each kernel of I⊗_A B→B at every q; if all local kernels vanish, the global kernel vanishes by prime support. The ideal criterion then gives flatness. Treat zero rings separately.

items.title: Flatness under base change
items.statement: Assume AC. Every base change of a flat scheme morphism is flat.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: On affine charts the pulled-back ring is B⊗_A A′. For every injection of A′-modules, view it as an A-injection, tensor first with flat B and use the tensor associativity isomorphism to obtain injectivity after tensoring with B⊗_A A′. Localize and glue.

items.title: Flatness under composition
items.statement: The composite of two flat morphisms of schemes is flat.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: At a point x→y→s, the local maps O_{S,s}→O_{Y,y}→O_{X,x} are flat. Apply transitivity for flat modules, including the zero case.

items.title: Faithfully flat scheme morphism
items.statement: A scheme morphism is faithfully flat if it is flat and surjective on underlying topological spaces. An fpqc morphism is a faithfully flat quasi-compact morphism, using the earlier fpqc definition.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.title: A flat local map is faithfully flat
items.statement: Assume AC. A flat local homomorphism of nonzero local rings is faithfully flat. Consequently the induced local-ring map at a flat point of a scheme morphism is faithfully flat. AC supplies containment of each proper ideal in the unique maximal ideal.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: For any proper ideal I⊂A, I⊂m and IB⊂n, so IB≠B. If an A-module N has N⊗_A B=0, select a nonzero cyclic subquotient A/I from a nonzero element and use flatness to inject its tensor into N⊗B; B/IB≠0 is a contradiction. This also proves exactness reflection after applying the same argument to homology modules.

items.title: Vanishing descends along an fpqc morphism
items.statement: Let f:X→S be fpqc and F any O_S-module. If f*F=0, then F=0. No quasi-coherence assumption is needed.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: For each s choose x over s; the stalk of f*F at x is F_s⊗_{O_{S,s}}O_{X,x}. The local flat map is faithful, so F_s=0. A sheaf with all stalks zero is zero. AC is used to select x for every s only if making all selections simultaneously; prove pointwise instead.

items.title: Generic freeness over a Noetherian domain
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If A is a Noetherian domain, B a finite-type A-algebra, and M a finite B-module, then M_a is a free A_a-module for some nonzero a∈A (possibly of infinite rank).

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Induct on algebra generators. For B[T], filter M by finite B-submodules M_n spanned by T^i times fixed finite generators for i≤n. The maps on successive quotients induced by T are surjective and stabilize to isomorphisms by Noetherianity of the first layer. Only finitely many quotient isomorphism types remain; choose one common nonzero localization making each free by induction. Split the resulting filtration degree by degree because free quotients are projective; its union is their direct sum. A quotient B[T]/I is handled by viewing M as a B[T]-module. This is Vakil §25.5.12 with the exercises supplied. AC is used for prime/maximal-ideal existence or the cited published algebraic result; no use is made of the incompatible deferred set-theory branch.

items.title: Generic flatness for finite-type morphisms
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let f:X→S be finite type with S integral Noetherian. There is a dense open U⊂S such that X_U→U is flat; U may meet components with empty fibres.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Cover the Noetherian base by finitely many affines and each quasi-compact inverse image by finitely many affine source charts. Apply generic freeness to each coordinate algebra as a module over itself, shrink each target affine by the finite product of its nonzero localizers, and take the union of these dense opens. On each source chart freeness implies flatness. AC is used for prime/maximal-ideal existence or the cited published algebraic result; no use is made of the incompatible deferred set-theory branch.

items.title: Constructible images for finite-presentation affine maps
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finitely presented ring map A→B and b∈B, the image of D(b)⊂Spec B in Spec A is constructible.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
The Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, §§10.29 and 10.125

items.strategy: Prove the stronger affine Chevalley statement that every constructible subset of Spec B has constructible image for every finitely presented A-algebra B. First note that a constructible subset is a finite union of D(f) intersect V(g_1,...,g_m) with the closed ideal finitely generated: a quasi-compact open is a finite union of basic opens, and constructible means a finite Boolean expression in them. Images under finite-presentation closed quotients and principal localizations preserve constructibility by pulling these finite Boolean expressions to Spec A. Factor A→B into finitely many polynomial extensions followed by the finite-presentation quotient, so it remains to treat projection Spec A[T]→Spec A on D(f)∩V(g_1,...,g_m). For no equations, write f=∑a_iT^i: over p the fibre D(f) is nonempty exactly when some a_i∉p, hence its image is ∪D(a_i). For one equation g with unit leading coefficient, C=A[T]/(g) is free of rank deg g, multiplication by f has characteristic polynomial T^d+∑r_iT^i, and the fibre D(f) is nonempty exactly when f is not nilpotent in C⊗κ(p), equivalently some r_i∉p; the image is ∪D(r_i). To reduce arbitrary g_i, cut Spec A into D(c) and V(c) for the leading coefficient c of a nonzero lowest-degree equation: on V(c) its degree falls; on D(c) divide the other equations by that equation to lower their degrees without changing their common zero set. Induct lexicographically on number and ordered degrees of equations; the two base cases were just computed. Every cut is finite and every image obtained is a finite Boolean combination of basic opens, so the induction works for an arbitrary base ring without Noetherian approximation. The AC assumption is used only when a nonzero fibre ring is assigned a prime, via prime-ideal existence. This is the constructive polynomial argument of Stacks Algebra 10.29.10, with its characteristic-polynomial and one-variable lemmas spelled out.

items.title: Constructible subsets stable under generalisation are open in an affine spectrum
items.statement: Assume AC. Let E be a constructible subset of Spec A. If E is stable under specialisation then E is closed; if E is stable under generalisation then E is open. Stability is taken with respect to the specialisation order on the spectrum.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Topology, Lemma 5.23.6 (tag 0903) and Section 5.19 (tags 0062, 0065)
The Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, Section 10.41 (tags 00HY, 00I0, 00I1)

items.title: Open and universally open morphisms of schemes
items.statement: A morphism of schemes f:X->S is open if the underlying map of topological spaces is an open map; it is universally open if for every S-scheme T the base-changed projection X x_S T -> T is open. The quantifier ranges over all S-schemes, with no finiteness hypothesis.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Definition 29.24.1 (tag 01U0)

items.title: Flat finite-presentation morphisms are open
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. A flat morphism locally of finite presentation is universally open.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
The Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, §§10.29 and 10.125

items.strategy: Cover source and target by affine opens and reduce the image of any source basic open D(b) to a finitely presented ring map A→B_b; the preceding affine Chevalley lemma makes this image constructible. If q∈Spec B_b lies over p and p′⊂p is a generalization, the local flat map A_p→(B_b)_q is faithfully flat by the local flat-map lemma. Tensor the nonzero local ring A_{p′}/p′ with (B_b)_q, or equivalently apply faithful flatness to the ideal p′A_p, to find a prime of (B_b)_q over p′A_p; its inverse image in B_b lies over p′. Thus the constructible image is stable under generalization. Prove the spectral-space criterion directly: on each quasi-compact basic open of Spec A, a constructible subset has finite locally closed stratification; if it is stable under generalization, its complement is constructible and specialization-stable and therefore closed by the standard quasi-compactness argument for spectral spaces. Hence the image of every D(b) is open and so is the image of any source open. Flatness and local finite presentation survive arbitrary base change, giving universal openness. AC enters the prime-existence step in the faithful-flat lifting argument.

items.title: Local fibre-dimension bound from polynomial quasi-finiteness
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let A→B be a finite-type ring map and q∈Spec B over p∈Spec A. If the dimension at q of Spec(B⊗_A κ(p)) is n, then there is g∈B\q and an A-algebra map A[T_1,…,T_n]→B_g that is quasi-finite. Consequently some open neighbourhood of q in Spec B has fibre-local dimension at most n at every point.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, §§10.29 and 10.125

items.strategy: Choose a principal open D(g) around the fibre point q whose entire fibre over p has dimension n, using the definition of local dimension and shrinking inside that fibre. Apply the published Noether normalisation construction to the finite-type κ(p)-algebra (B_g)⊗κ(p). Its triangular polynomial substitutions can be chosen as integral polynomials in a finite list of algebra generators; lift these polynomial expressions to y_1,…,y_n∈B_g. The induced map A[T_1,…,T_n]→B_g has finite fibre at q, hence is quasi-finite at q. The published affine local Zariski Main theorem gives an open neighbourhood of q on which this map factors as an open subspace of a finite algebra, so shrink D(g) once more to make it quasi-finite throughout. At every q′ of this open, pass to the κ(p′)-fibre. An affine quasi-finite map from that fibre to affine n-space is locally an open part of a finite integral extension; the published incomparability/dimension theorem bounds its local dimension by n. Thus all q′ in the resulting neighbourhood have local fibre dimension ≤n. Prime selection, Noether normalisation, and local Zariski Main use the declared AC assumption.

items.title: Upper semicontinuity of proper fibre dimension
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a proper finite-type f:X→S, with dim empty fibre defined as −∞, the set {s:dim X_s≥n} is closed for every n≥0.

references.title: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms §§37.22, 37.30, 37.41–44
Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37

items.strategy: For every d≥0, the preceding local fibre-dimension lemma makes U_d={x∈X:dim_x X_{f(x)}≤d} open on a finite-type source. Its complement Z_d is closed. Properness makes f(Z_d) closed in S. A fibre has dimension >d exactly when it meets Z_d, so {s:dim X_s>d}=f(Z_d) is closed. The empty fibre has value −∞ and is handled by the same equivalence. AC is inherited from the local dimension bound and prime-existence steps.

items.title: Smooth morphism of schemes
items.statement: A morphism f:X→S is smooth at x if it is locally of finite presentation at x, flat at x, and the fibre over s=f(x) is geometrically regular at x (after every extension of κ(s)); f is smooth if so at every x. Empty fibres impose no pointwise condition.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.title: Relative dimension for a smooth morphism
items.statement: A smooth morphism has relative dimension n at x if its geometric fibre has local dimension n at x. It has pure relative dimension n if every nonempty geometric fibre is pure n-dimensional. On a standard smooth chart the dimension is the number of variables minus the number of independent equations.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.title: Smoothness survives base change and composition
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Smooth morphisms of schemes are stable under arbitrary base change and composition. On compatible standard charts their relative dimensions add under composition.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Replace flat-geometrically-regular charts by local standard-smooth presentations using the published algebra equivalence. Tensor the equations and invertible Jacobian minor for base change. For composition clear denominators and form the block triangular Jacobian with invertible diagonal blocks; the published algebra theorem supplies this calculation. Pass from ring charts to schemes by affine localization. AC is used for prime/maximal-ideal existence or the cited published algebraic result; no use is made of the incompatible deferred set-theory branch.

items.title: Smoothness and formal smoothness
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. A scheme morphism is smooth iff it is locally of finite presentation and formally smooth in the local lifting convention of the earlier definition.

references.title: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms §§37.8, 37.11

items.strategy: Work at each x with affine charts R→B=R[T_1,...,T_n]/I, where I is finitely generated. Smooth⇒formal smooth: on a standard-smooth localization choose lifts of T_i across a square-zero ideal, compute the errors f_j(tilde T), and solve the linear correction equations using an invertible Jacobian minor; after shrinking the affine test around its points this supplies the local lift required by the stated convention. Conversely, a local lift for the square-zero thickening Spec(P/I²) of Spec B gives, near x, a section of P/I²→B. Write the local section as T_i↦T_i−g_i modulo I² with g_i∈I. For f∈I, the congruence f(T−g)=0 modulo I² gives f≡∑_i(∂f/∂T_i)g_i modulo I². Thus the B-linear map B^n→I/I² sending dT_i to g_i modulo I² retracts the conormal map I/I²→B^n, making that map split injective; its cokernel Ω_{B/R} is projective. Since I is finitely generated, at x choose r generators whose conormal classes form a basis of its projective direct summand and choose r coordinates for which the Jacobian r×r minor is a unit. Local Nakayama applied to I/(f_1,...,f_r) in the local polynomial ring shows the selected equations generate I after shrinking near x. The resulting presentation is standard smooth at x. The published algebraic standard-smooth/geometrically-regular equivalence then gives flatness, locally finite presentation and geometrically regular fibres, so f is smooth. The argument uses the local test lifting convention throughout; no global torsor or H¹ vanishing is needed. AC is used in selection of local primes and bases, not to infer a global lift.

items.title: Relative Jacobian criterion with its presentation hypothesis
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a locally finitely presented f:X→S, f is smooth at x iff near x it has some presentation as an open of Spec(A[t_1,…,t_m]/(f_1,…,f_r)) over Spec A with an r×r Jacobian minor invertible at x. Such a chart is flat with geometrically regular fibres of dimension m−r. The criterion does not demand that every redundant equation list have such a minor.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: A unit Jacobian minor is the standard-smooth algebra condition, whose flatness and geometric regularity are proved in the earlier algebra page. Conversely that page’s local-presentation theorem produces some regular sequence of equations and an invertible minor after shrinking; track the presentation chosen and do not apply the assertion to an arbitrary redundant equation list. AC is used for prime/maximal-ideal existence or the cited published algebraic result; no use is made of the incompatible deferred set-theory branch.

items.title: Differentials of a smooth morphism
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If f:X→S is smooth of pure relative dimension n, then Ω_{X/S} is locally free of rank n. More generally its rank at x is the local relative dimension.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: On a standard chart the conormal presentation gives a cokernel of the r×m Jacobian. Invert the r×r minor and perform row-column elimination; the remaining m−r differential classes form a basis. Sheafify and compare with the local relative dimension; no left injectivity of a general conormal sequence is assumed. AC is used for prime/maximal-ideal existence or the cited published algebraic result; no use is made of the incompatible deferred set-theory branch.

items.title: Fibres of a smooth morphism are smooth
items.statement: Every ordinary or geometric fibre of a smooth morphism is smooth over its residue field, including empty fibres vacuously.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Base change to Spec κ(s) and then to any extension field. Smoothness survives both base changes; over a field, the standard smooth chart is geometrically regular by the published algebra result.

items.title: Étale morphism of schemes
items.statement: A morphism is étale at x if it is smooth at x of relative dimension zero, and étale if this holds everywhere. Thus it is locally of finite presentation, flat, and has geometrically regular zero-dimensional fibres.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.title: Etale neighbourhoods and elementary etale neighbourhoods of a point
items.statement: Let S be a scheme and s a point of S. An etale neighbourhood of (S,s) is a pair (U,u) with U a scheme, phi:U->S an etale morphism and u a point of U with phi(u)=s; a morphism of etale neighbourhoods is a morphism of S-schemes preserving the chosen points. The neighbourhood is elementary if the residue field map kappa(s)->kappa(u) is an isomorphism (kappa(u)=kappa(s)). No affineness of U and no closedness of u is required. An open neighbourhood U subset S of s, with its inclusion, is an etale neighbourhood and is elementary; compositions of etale neighbourhoods are etale neighbourhoods, and compositions of elementary ones are elementary.

references.title: The Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, Definition 37.35.1 (tag 02LE) and Section 37.35
The Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Section 29.37

items.title: Smooth maps have étale local affine-space form
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a smooth f:X→S of relative dimension n at x, after shrinking an affine source neighbourhood, there is an étale S-morphism U→A^n_S whose composite with A^n_S→S is f|_U; the target need only be shrunk Zariski locally.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Take a standard-smooth presentation with r equations in n+r variables and an invertible r×r Jacobian minor. Projection onto the remaining n variables has a square Jacobian presentation with invertible determinant; verify it is étale by the flat-and-unramified criterion below, or prove this directly from the block Jacobian algebra to avoid a forward dependency. The factorization holds on the principal source chart. AC is used for prime/maximal-ideal existence or the cited published algebraic result; no use is made of the incompatible deferred set-theory branch.

items.title: Étale equals flat and unramified in finite presentation
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a locally finitely presented morphism f:X→S, f is étale at x iff it is flat and unramified at x. Here unramified means vanishing Ω_{X/S} at x with residue-field separability then following from finite type and zero differentials.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: On a standard smooth chart the zero-dimensional condition makes the square Jacobian matrix invertible; hence Ω=0 and the residue extension is finite separable. Conversely, for a finitely presented flat algebra with Ω at q zero and separable residue, the fibre local ring is a zero-dimensional geometrically regular field extension; the published standard-smooth equivalence yields smoothness. Track the separability hypothesis: Ω=0 alone over imperfect fields does not imply geometric regularity. AC is used for prime/maximal-ideal existence or the cited published algebraic result; no use is made of the incompatible deferred set-theory branch.

items.title: Etale morphisms are the formally etale morphisms locally of finite presentation
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. A morphism is étale iff it is locally of finite presentation and formally étale in the unique local lifting convention of the earlier definition.

references.title: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms §§37.8, 37.11

items.strategy: For étale f, smoothness gives local lifts by the preceding criterion. Formal unramifiedness, equivalently Ω_{X/S}=0 on affine charts, makes two lifts across a square-zero ideal agree: their difference is an S-derivation into that ideal, and the universal property of Ω kills it. Thus f is formally étale. Conversely, formal étaleness includes formal smoothness, so locally finite presentation plus the preceding smooth criterion makes f smooth. Uniqueness of lifts applied to the two maps B→B⊕M with the same reduction forces every R-derivation B→M to vanish for every B-module M; taking M=Ω_{B/R} and the universal derivation yields Ω_{B/R}=0. On a smooth standard chart Ω is locally free of rank equal to the relative dimension, so rank zero makes every nonempty geometric fibre zero-dimensional; f is étale by its definition. AC is only inherited from the smooth criterion and the field/prime selections in its standard-chart theorem.

items.title: Étale stability
items.statement: Étale morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change and composition.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Use smooth stability and the standard chart dimension count. Relative dimension zero remains zero on base change and adds to zero under composition, including empty fibres.

items.title: Étale maps are open and locally quasi-finite
items.statement: An étale morphism is universally open and locally quasi-finite; a quasi-compact étale morphism is quasi-finite in the finite-type fibre sense.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Étale means smooth of relative dimension zero, hence flat and locally of finite presentation. The flat finite-presentation openness theorem applies after every base change, proving universal openness. At any x over s, the finite-type κ(s)-fibre is zero-dimensional at x, so x is isolated in that fibre and its residue field is a finite extension of κ(s); the quasi-finite-at-a-point criterion in the declared quasi-finite definition makes f locally quasi-finite. If f is quasi-compact, cover the source over each affine target chart by finitely many finite-type affine charts. Each zero-dimensional fibre of one such affine chart is an Artinian finite-type κ(s)-algebra and has finitely many points. The finite cover gives finite fibres and finite type globally, hence quasi-finite. The two claims deliberately keep local and global quasi-finiteness distinct.

items.title: Standard étale algebra
items.statement: An A-algebra is standard étale if it is (A[T]/(P))_g where P∈A[T] is monic and P′ is a unit in that localization; equivalently some power of g lies in the ideal (P′) of A[T]/(P). The monic requirement makes A[T]/(P) finite free before localization; the resulting localized algebra need not be finite over A.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26
Stacks Project, Algebra §10.144, Proposition 10.144.4

items.strategy: This is the Stacks §10.144.1 convention; note that (A[T]/P)_g can be étale without this exact normal form before changing presentation.

items.title: Every étale morphism has standard étale charts
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For an étale f:X→S and x∈X, there are affine neighbourhoods U of x and V of f(x) with f(U)⊂V such that O(U) is a standard étale O(V)-algebra after possibly further localization.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26
Stacks Project, Algebra §10.144, Proposition 10.144.4

items.strategy: Fix q over p on affine R→B and shrink around q so B is finitely presented étale. Étaleness makes the fibre at q a finite separable field κ(q)/κ(p) and makes the finite-type map quasi-finite there. Apply the published affine Zariski Main local factorization to replace B near q by a localization of a finite R-algebra C that is still étale at q. The finite κ(p)-algebra C⊗κ(p) is Artinian: split it into local factors, with the selected factor κ(q). By the published primitive-element theorem choose a nonzero α generating κ(q)/κ(p), set tbar=(α,0,...,0) in this product, and lift a nonzero scalar multiple to t∈C after shrinking R near p. Put C′=R[t]⊂C. The selected prime q is the only prime of C over its contraction q′ in C′, and the finite local map C′_{q′}→C_q has the same residue field and closed fibre κ(q); Nakayama makes it surjective, so it is an isomorphism. Shrink at q to replace C by the one-generator finite algebra C′=R[T]/I. In κ(p)[T], the fibre ideal Iκ(p)[T] has a monic generator hbar with selected factor hbar_1 the separable minimal polynomial of α; lift a nonzero scalar multiple of hbar to h∈I after localizing R at an element outside p. Since t is integral, I contains a monic m. For l≥2 with l deg m>deg h, f=m^l+h is monic and belongs to I. In the residue polynomial ring fbar=hbar_1 wbar, with gcd(hbar_1,wbar)=1 because hbar contains hbar_1 only to exponent one while mbar contains every fibre factor; thus f′ is invertible at q. The surjection R[T]/(f)→C′ becomes, after inverting f′ and shrinking around q, a surjection between two étale R-algebras. Such a map is formally étale over its source by uniqueness/existence of R-lifts and hence étale by the preceding finite-presentation criterion; a surjective étale ring map is locally an idempotent quotient, so after localizing at the selected point it is an isomorphism. The resulting R[T]_{fg}/(f) chart is standard étale. The argument treats inseparable-residue cases by their exclusion from étaleness, and the nonzero α choice covers even the trivial residue extension. AC is declared for prime, primitive-element and finite-product choices.

items.title: Finite étale schemes over an algebraically closed field
items.statement: Assume AC. Every finite-type etale scheme over an algebraically closed field k is a finite disjoint union of Spec k and is finite over k, uniquely up to permutation. Conversely every finite disjoint union is finite etale. An infinite disjoint union is etale but not quasi-compact or finite type; these identity-component examples are choice-free.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: A finite k-algebra is Artinian. Étale implies reduced zero-dimensional fibres and separable residue fields, which equal k. The reduced Artinian algebra therefore splits as k^r. Conversely each factor is standard étale and finite products give a finite étale map. The distinction between finite and locally finite type is essential.

items.title: Smooth locus of a morphism
items.statement: For a locally finitely presented f:X→S, the smooth locus Sm(f) is the set of x∈X where f is smooth at x.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.title: The smooth locus is open
items.statement: For a locally finitely presented morphism f:X→S, Sm(f) is open in X and its restriction is a smooth morphism.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: At each smooth point take a standard-smooth affine chart with an invertible Jacobian minor. Its principal-open neighbourhood consists of smooth points because the same determinant stays invertible. The union of those charts is exactly Sm(f).

items.title: Étale locus of a morphism
items.statement: For a locally finitely presented f:X→S, the étale locus Et(f) is the set of points where f is étale.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.title: The étale locus is open
items.statement: For a locally finitely presented morphism f:X→S, Et(f) is open in X and its restriction is étale.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26
Stacks Project, Algebra §10.144, Proposition 10.144.4

items.strategy: At an étale point the standard smooth chart has relative dimension zero, so its chosen Jacobian minor is square and invertible. On the corresponding principal open the same chart remains standard smooth with zero free differential rank. Hence every point in that open is étale; the union of such opens is Et(f).

items.title: Classical and scheme smoothness over a perfect field
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be a perfect field and X a finite-type k-scheme. A classical smooth k-variety in the earlier variety convention has smooth structure morphism X→Spec k. Conversely a reduced finite-type k-scheme with smooth structure morphism is classically smooth at every point; if the earlier convention requires irreducibility, add irreducibility separately.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Over a perfect field, regular local finite-type k-algebras are geometrically regular. Match the earlier classical local Jacobian criterion to a standard-smooth chart and apply the published regular-equals-smooth result. Check separately that irreducibility or connectedness is a variety convention rather than a smoothness consequence. The AV-6 A page is now a direct in-run prerequisite; its two classical smoothness suppliers must be authored and independently audited before use. AC is used for prime/maximal-ideal existence or the cited published algebraic result; no use is made of the incompatible deferred set-theory branch.

items.title: Fibrewise injectivity lifts and leaves a flat cokernel over a Noetherian target
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism of local rings with $S$ Noetherian, and write $\mathfrak m$ for the maximal ideal of $R$. Let $M$ be an $S$-module flat over $R$, let $N$ be a finite $S$-module, and let $u:N\to M$ be $S$-linear. If the fibre map $N/\mathfrak mN\to M/\mathfrak mM$ is injective, then $u$ is injective and $\operatorname{coker}(u)$ is flat over $R$. No Noetherian or finite-generation condition is imposed on $R$ or on $M$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.99.1 (tag 00ME), fibre-injective maps

items.strategy: lift the injection through every power of the maximal ideal, use Krull intersection, then repeat modulo arbitrary ideals to test flatness of the cokernel.

items.title: A finite module with free fibre and flat base is free over a Noetherian target
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset R$, and let $M$ be a nonzero finite $S$-module. If $M$ is flat over $R$ and $M/\mathfrak mM$ is free over $S/\mathfrak mS$, then $M$ is a finite free $S$-module and $S$ is flat over $R$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.99.4 (tag 00MH), free fibre and flatness

items.strategy: lift a fibre basis, use fibrewise injection and Nakayama, and recover flatness of the middle ring as a summand.

items.title: The flat locus of a finitely presented algebra is open
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). Let $R\to B$ be a finitely presented ring map ([[def-finitely-presented-module-and-algebra]]). Then the set of primes $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ at which $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}B$. The same statement holds with a finitely presented $B$-module $M$ in place of $B$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, openness of flatness

items.strategy: Descend the finitely presented pair to a Noetherian stage where flatness holds. Regard the module over a polynomial chart, take the finite nth syzygy in a finite-free resolution, and use Tor plus regular polynomial fibre global dimension to make that syzygy free near the chosen point. The fibrewise exact-complex openness lemma spreads exactness; the flat-complex lifting lemma makes the module flat on the resulting neighbourhood. Base change from the Noetherian stage proves the general case.

items.title: Local flatness criterion for a module finite over a larger Noetherian local algebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, let $I\subsetneq R$ be an ideal, and let $M$ be a finite $S$-module. If $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ and the multiplication map $$I\otimes_R M\longrightarrow M$$ is injective, then $M$ is flat over $R$. There is **no** assumption that $M$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.99.10 (tag 00ML), variant of the local criterion
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.99.7 (tag 00MK), local criterion for flatness

items.strategy: lift a relation modulo $I$ to get the maximal-ideal injection, then use finite-length Tor vanishing and Artin–Rees to test all ideals.

items.title: Finite presentation data descend to Noetherian algebra and module stages
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R\to S$ be a finitely presented ring map, and let $M$ be a finitely presented $S$-module. There is a directed system $(R_i\to S_i,M_i)$ with the following properties. 1. Each $R_i$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra, each $S_i$ is a finitely presented $R_i$-algebra, and each $M_i$ is a finitely presented $S_i$-module. In particular the stage rings are Noetherian. 2. For $i\le j$, the maps $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to S_j$ and $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j\to M_j$ are isomorphisms. The colimits are $R$, $S$, and $M$, respectively. 3. For primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq S$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$, write $\mathfrak p_i=\mathfrak p\cap R_i$ and $\mathfrak q_i=\mathfrak q\cap S_i$. Then $(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}\to(S_i)_{\mathfrak q_i}$ is a system of Noetherian local maps with colimit $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$, and the localized modules have colimit $M_{\mathfrak q}$. For $i\le j$, $(S_i)_{\mathfrak q_i}\otimes_{(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}} (R_j)_{\mathfrak p_j}\to(S_j)_{\mathfrak q_j}$ is a localization, and the corresponding module transition is base change. This lemma constructs the approximating system. It does not assert that flatness at the colimit descends to a finite stage.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.127.18 (tag 00R1), finite-presentation approximation
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.127.13 (tag 00QX), local approximation with modules

items.strategy: put all finite coefficients in one stage and

items.title: A killed first Tor obstruction yields flatness after local Noetherian base change
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Consider a commutative square of local homomorphisms of Noetherian local rings $$\begin{array}{ccc}R&\longrightarrow&R'\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ S&\longrightarrow&S'\end{array}$$ such that $S'$ is a localization of $S\otimes_RR'$. Let $I\subsetneq R$, put $I'=IR'$, let $M$ be a finite $S$-module, and put $M'=M\otimes_SS'$. Assume $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$ and the natural map $$\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/I,M)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tor}_1^{R'}(R'/I',M')$$ is zero. Then $M'$ is flat over $R'$. The first Tor group is the kernel of $I\otimes_RM\to M$; thus the hypothesis says that this original obstruction dies after the indicated base change. The module $M$ need only be finite over $S$, never over $R$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.99.14 (tag 00MO), Tor-killing base-change criterion
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.99.12 (tag 00MM), first Tor comparison
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.99.13 (tag 00MN), second Tor comparison

items.strategy: prove the two first-Tor comparison surjections by finite degrees of free resolutions, then apply the local criterion.

items.title: Flatness over a local filtered colimit appears at a Noetherian stage
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(R_i\to S_i,M_i)$ be a directed system of Noetherian local ring maps and finite $S_i$-modules. For $i\le j$, suppose $S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to S_j$ is a localization and $M_i\otimes_{S_i}S_j\to M_j$ is an isomorphism. Write $R=\varinjlim R_i$, $S=\varinjlim S_i$, and $M=\varinjlim M_i$. If $M$ is flat over $R$, then $M_j$ is flat over $R_j$ at some stage $j$. In particular this applies to the localized approximation system of [[lem-noetherian-approximation-fp-algebra-module-system]].

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.128.3 (tag 00R6), eventual flatness
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.127.13 (tag 00QX), local approximation

items.strategy: kill finitely many generators of the first Tor obstruction at a finite stage, then use the local flatness criterion.

items.title: Noetherian fibrewise flatness for a module finite over the target
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R\to S\to S'$ be local homomorphisms of Noetherian local rings, and let $M$ be a finite $S'$-module. Write $\mathfrak m$ for the maximal ideal of $R$. If $M$ is flat over $R$ and $M/\mathfrak mM$ is flat over $S/\mathfrak mS$, then $M$ is flat over $S$. The conclusion also holds when $M=0$. No finiteness of $M$ over $R$ or $S$ is assumed. This is the module-flatness conclusion of Stacks Lemma 10.99.15; its additional conclusion that $S$ is flat over $R$ is not needed here.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.99.15 (tag 00MP), Noetherian fibrewise flatness criterion

items.strategy: transfer the ideal-tensor injection along the middle ring, then apply the finite-over-target local criterion.

items.title: Flatness over a polynomial chart from base and fibre flatness
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let R→P=R[T_1,…,T_d]→B be ring maps with B a finitely presented P-algebra. At a prime q of B over p of R, if B_q is flat over R_p and the closed-fibre local algebra (B⊗_R κ(p))_q is flat over κ(p)[T_1,…,T_d] at the induced prime, then B_q is flat over P at q.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, critère de platitude par fibres

items.strategy: Localize R,P,B at the three indicated primes. First assume the rings are Noetherian. Put I=pP. Because P=R[T] is R-flat, the canonical map p⊗_R B→I⊗_P B is surjective. Its composite with I⊗_P B→B is the multiplication map p⊗_R B→B, injective by R-flatness, so I⊗_P B→B is injective and Tor_1^P(P/I,B)=0. The assumed closed-fibre flatness says B/IB is flat over P/I. Apply the local flatness criterion for a Noetherian local map P→B with finite B-module M=B: use the equational flatness criterion to lift finite relations modulo I, and the just-established Tor vanishing to kill the correction in I; Nakayama on the finite relation module closes the lift. This gives B flat over P. For arbitrary R, write the localized finitely presented data as a filtered colimit of local essentially finite-type Z-algebras R_i and finitely presented P_i→B_i. The Tor_1 module controlling R_i-flatness at the chosen point is finite over the Noetherian B_i; its generators vanish in the colimit because B is R-flat, hence at a later stage. Repeat for the closed-fibre Tor_1 module controlling (B_i/p_iB_i)-flatness over P_i/p_iP_i. The local flatness criterion at each stage turns these finite Tor vanishings into the two flatness hypotheses of the Noetherian case. Apply that case at the common later stage and base-change back to R. This is the finite-presentation descent in Stacks Algebra 10.128; each use of AC is in prime selection or finite generator choice.

items.title: Dense relative-dimension strata in flat finitely presented fibres
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f\colon X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes that is flat ([[def-flat-morphism-schemes]]) and locally of finite presentation ([[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]). For $x\in X$ put $s=f(x)$, let $X_s$ denote the scheme-theoretic fibre ([[def-scheme-theoretic-fibre]]) and let $\dim_xX_s$ be its local dimension at $x$ ([[def-relative-dimension-smooth-morphism]]). Write $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ for the local ring of the fibre at $x$ ([[def-local-ring]]) and put $$W=\{x\in X:\mathcal O_{X_s,x}\text{ is Cohen--Macaulay}\}$$ ([[def-cohen-macaulay-local-module-and-ring]]), and for $d\ge0$ $$W_d=\{x\in W:\dim_xX_s=d\}.$$ Then: 1. every fibre $X_s$ is a locally Noetherian scheme, and $W$ is open in $X$; 2. $W\cap X_s$ is dense in $X_s$, for every $s\in S$; 3. each $W_d$ is open in $X$; the sets $W_d$ are pairwise disjoint and $W=\bigsqcup_{d\ge0}W_d$; and for every $s\in S$ with $X_s\ne\varnothing$, $$\sup\{d\ge0:W_d\cap X_s\ne\varnothing\}=\dim X_s\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}.$$ If $\dim X_s$ is finite, this supremum is a largest attained value. The finite presentation case is included, since finite presentation implies local finite presentation ([[def-finitely-presented-module-and-algebra]], [[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]). No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $S$, and no separatedness, reducedness or quasi-compactness is used.

references.title: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms §§37.22, 37.30, 37.41–44
Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37

items.strategy: Use field-fibre dimension and Cohen–Macaulay parameter arguments to make a quasi-finite polynomial chart flat at a chosen point, then spread flatness by the locally proved flat-locus theorem. The resulting open charts have constant local fibre dimension; generic component points give density and the supremum formula, including unbounded fibres.

items.title: Lower semicontinuity of flat finitely presented fibre dimension
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to S$ be flat and of finite presentation. For $s\in S$, let $X_s$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre ([[def-scheme-theoretic-fibre]]), with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$. Then, for every integer $n\ge0$, the set $$D_n=\{s\in S:\dim X_s\ge n\}$$ is open in $S$. Thus the fibre-dimension function is lower semicontinuous.

references.title: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms §§37.22, 37.30, 37.41–44
Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37

items.strategy: The strata lemma gives open W_d whose labels meet every nonempty fibre with supremum equal to its dimension. Since flat locally finitely presented morphisms are open, each image f(W_d) is open; D_n is their union for d≥n.

items.title: Fibre dimension of proper flat finitely presented families
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If $f:X\to S$ is proper, flat, and of finite presentation, then the function $$s\longmapsto\dim X_s\in\{-\infty\}\cup\mathbb N$$ is locally constant on $S$, where $X_s$ is the scheme-theoretic fibre and $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$ ([[def-scheme-theoretic-fibre]]). In particular the empty-fibre locus is open and closed. No assertion is made for arbitrary flat families.

references.title: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms §§37.22, 37.30, 37.41–44
Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37

items.strategy: Lower semicontinuity makes each dimension threshold open. Proper upper semicontinuity makes each threshold closed. Differences of successive thresholds are open level sets, including the empty-fibre and dimension-zero cases.

items.title: Flatness does not identify fibres
items.statement: Over Q, flatness does not force smoothness or isomorphic fibres: the finite free family Spec Q[t,x]/(x²−t)→A¹_Q has a nonreduced fibre at t=0 and a reduced two-point fibre at t=1.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: As a Q[t]-module, Q[t,x]/(x²−t) has basis 1,x, hence is free and flat. Base change to t=0 gives Q[x]/(x²), which has a nonzero nilpotent; base change to t=1 gives Q[x]/((x−1)(x+1))≅Q×Q via evaluation at ±1, with inverse (a,b)↦(a+b)/2+(a−b)x/2. Thus the fibres are not isomorphic, and the special fibre is not smooth. No fibre-dimension theorem is needed.

items.title: Coprime fibre factorizations lift after an elementary étale base change
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let f∈R[T] be monic and p∈Spec R. If f modulo p factors in κ(p)[T] as a product of two coprime monic polynomials, then after an étale R-algebra R′ with a prime p′ over p and κ(p′)=κ(p), f factors in R′[T] as a product of monic coprime lifts.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, Lemma 10.143.13

items.strategy: Let the desired factors have degrees r,s and introduce coefficient variables b_1,…,b_r,c_1,…,c_s for monic polynomials g,h. Impose the r+s equations equating the coefficients of gh with those of f; this defines a finitely presented R-algebra R′. The given factorization defines a κ(p)-point p′ of Spec R′ with κ(p′)=κ(p). The Jacobian of the coefficient equations is the Sylvester matrix of gbar,hbar: varying the factors gives δg·hbar+gbar·δh, and uniqueness of the division algorithm shows this linear map on polynomials of degree <r and <s is invertible exactly when gcd(gbar,hbar)=1. Equivalently its determinant is the nonzero resultant. The local square-Jacobian criterion makes R→R′ étale at p′; invert the determinant to make it étale on the chosen chart. The universal coefficient equations give f=gh there. The adjugate of the Sylvester matrix writes 1 as a combination of g and h after the same localization, so they are coprime. AC is declared for choosing p and the algebraic closure used by the published resultant criterion.

items.title: Finite neighbourhood of an isolated fibre point after elementary étale change
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If f:X→S is locally of finite type and x∈X_s is isolated in its fibre, there is an elementary étale neighbourhood (U,u)→(S,s) with κ(u)=κ(s) and an open V⊂X_U containing the point over x such that V→U is finite and V_u consists of that one point with its original residue field. No separatedness is needed for this open finite neighbourhood.

references.title: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms §§37.22, 37.30, 37.41–44
Stacks Project, Algebra §10.143, Lemma 10.143.13
Stacks Project, Algebra §10.145, Lemma 10.145.2

items.strategy: Reduce around x and s to a finite-type affine A→B with q over p. Let B_int⊂B be the relative integral closure of A. Published affine local Zariski Main gives g∈B_int\q with (B_int)_g≅B_g. In the fibre of B_int at p, the point q_int is closed because the algebra is integral over κ(p), and isolated because D(g) identifies a neighbourhood with the isolated finite-type fibre point q. Thus the singleton {q_int} is clopen in the fibre; split the fibre ring by an idempotent, and lift a scalar multiple of that idempotent to t∈B_int with t nonzero at q_int and zero at every other point above p. Choose a monic annihilating polynomial F(T)∈A[T] for t. Its reduction factors as T^eHbar with Hbar(0)≠0; multiply F by T if needed to ensure e≥1. The coprime-factorization lifting lemma gives an elementary étale A→A′ with unchanged residue field and F=IH in A′[T], where I reduces to T^e, H to Hbar, and (I,H)=1. Evaluating at t gives orthogonal idempotents and splits A′⊗_A B into a factor C supported over q and a complementary factor. In the integral-closure factor C_int corresponding to C, the old g avoids its unique point over p. The image of V(g) under the integral map Spec C_int→Spec A′ is closed and misses p′, so after shrinking A′ near p′, g is invertible throughout C_int. The isomorphism (C_int)_g≅C_g then makes C finite over A′, since it is both integral and finite type. The clopen factor Spec C is the desired open finite neighbourhood, with a unique point over p′ mapping to x and unchanged residue field. All prime/idempotent selections use the declared AC assumption.

items.title: Elementary étale finite-component decomposition
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let f:X→S be separated and locally of finite type, s∈S, and x_1,…,x_n∈X_s distinct isolated points. There is an elementary étale neighbourhood (U,u)→(S,s) with κ(u)=κ(s) and a decomposition X×_S U=W⊔V_1⊔⋯⊔V_n into open-and-closed subschemes, each V_i finite over U with singleton fibre {v_i} over u, κ(v_i)=κ(x_i), and W_u containing no point mapping to any x_i. This is the exact Stacks 37.41.4 form.

references.title: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms §§37.22, 37.30, 37.41–44

items.strategy: Apply the preceding finite-neighbourhood lemma successively to the isolated points (Stacks 37.41.2); elementary étale base changes preserve the residue fields and earlier finite opens. Because X_U is separated and each V_i→U finite and proper, the proper-source-to-separated-target lemma makes V_i closed in X_U. Each V_i∩V_j is finite over U and avoids u; proper closed image permits shrinking U until the V_i are disjoint. Their open-and-closed union has open-and-closed complement W with the stated fibre property. AC is used for prime/maximal-ideal existence or the cited published algebraic result; no use is made of the incompatible deferred set-theory branch.

items.title: Quasi-compact quasi-separated structure pushforward is affine-local
items.statement: If f:X→S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then for every affine U=Spec R⊂S, the R-algebra M=Γ(f^{-1}U,O_X) localizes to Γ(f^{-1}D(r),O_X) for every r∈R. Hence f_*O_X is an affine-local quasi-coherent O_S-algebra; the same finite-cover argument gives flat base change for these sections.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, normalization construction

items.strategy: Over U=Spec R choose finitely many affine opens U_i covering X_U, possible by quasi-compactness. Quasi-separatedness makes each U_i∩U_j quasi-compact; cover it by finitely many affine opens U_ijk. The sheaf equalizer identifies Γ(X_U,O) with the kernel of ∏_iΓ(U_i,O)⇉∏_ijkΓ(U_ijk,O). R-localization is exact and commutes with these finite products. Each affine chart V in this display has V∩f^{-1}D(r)=D(r|_V), whose sections equal Γ(V,O)_r. The localized equalizer is therefore exactly the equalizer computing Γ(X_{D(r)},O), proving the claimed isomorphism. For any flat R→R′, tensor with R′ is exact and commutes with the same finite products; after base change the affine charts and pairwise affine refinements remain affine, so the equalizer also gives Γ(X_U,O)⊗_R R′≅Γ(X_U×_R R′,O). These localization isomorphisms are compatible with restriction and multiplication, so f_*O_X is the claimed algebra.

items.title: Integral closure commutes with étale base change
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For ring maps R→B and an étale R-algebra E, if A⊂B is the set of elements integral over the image of R, then E⊗_R A identifies with the integral closure of E in E⊗_R B.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Commutative Algebra, integral closure and smooth base change

items.strategy: Flatness of E/R injects E⊗A into E⊗B; its image is integral over E. Check the converse after a Zariski cover of Spec E by standard-étale charts E=(R[T]/F)_g, F monic and F′ invertible. Localizing integral closures reduces to R[T]/F. Let b in (B[T]/F) be integral over R[T]/F; since T is integral over R, b is integral over R. Adjoin all roots α_i of F one by one to B by monic quotients; the resulting B′ is finite free and faithfully injects B. If b is represented by ∑_{j<d}b_jT^j, the universal polynomial identity F′b=∑_i b(α_i)∏_{k≠i}(T−α_k) in B′[T]/F holds even for repeated roots, by proving it first over the polynomial ring with independent formal roots. Each α_i and each b(α_i) is integral over R, so every coefficient of this degree-<d expression is integral over R; uniqueness of the monic-basis representation shows those coefficients actually lie in B, hence in A. After inverting F′ we have b∈E⊗A. Descent from the standard-étale cover by localization proves equality globally. AC is declared for prime selection in the standard-étale covering; the finite free root-adjoining construction itself is explicit.

items.title: Integral quasi-coherent algebras over qcqs bases are unions of finite subalgebras
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. On a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme S, every integral affine-local quasi-coherent O_S-algebra is the filtered union of its finite quasi-coherent O_S-subalgebras. A finite set of local sections and their monic integrality certificates is contained in one such subalgebra after passing to a finite affine cover.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, integral algebra finite-subalgebra lemma

items.strategy: First prove the finite-type quasi-coherent submodule extension step. For a quasi-compact open U⊂S, a finite-type submodule G⊂F|_U extends inside a quasi-coherent F over qcqs S: add finitely many affine opens one at a time. On an affine new piece V, the quasi-compact overlap U∩V has a finite principal cover; extend G as a possibly infinite quasi-coherent submodule using the kernel of F⊕j_*G→j_*F|_{U∩V}, where j is the quasi-compact open inclusion; the same finite-affine equalizer argument as the preceding qcqs pushforward lemma proves these module pushforwards quasi-coherent. On each principal open of the overlap select finitely many module generators, clear denominators, and take their finite span in Γ(V,F); it has exactly G on the overlap. Glue to the existing G on U. By this extension lemma, every section of a quasi-coherent F on an affine open belongs to a global finite-type quasi-coherent submodule; sums make these submodules filtered. Apply this to the underlying module of the integral algebra A. The image in A of the symmetric algebra on each finite-type submodule is a finite-type quasi-coherent subalgebra, and images of two such subalgebras are contained in the image generated by their sum, so they form a filtered union equal to A. Each finite-type subalgebra is finite as an O_S-module because its finitely many local generators satisfy monic equations over the base; reduce powers successively using those equations on each affine chart. On a finite affine cover, finitely many sections and certificates are thus caught by one common finite subalgebra. AC is used to select finite covers and generators where needed.

items.title: An étale universally injective morphism is an open immersion
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (). If a morphism of schemes $f:X\to Y$ is étale () and universally injective, then it is an open immersion (). It is enough for universal injectivity that $f$ be injective on underlying points and induce an isomorphism $\kappa(f(x))\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(x)$ for every $x\in X$. No separatedness or quasi-compactness of $f$ or $Y$ is assumed.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Étale Morphisms of Schemes, Theorem 41.14.1 (tag 025F)
references.locator: Theorem 41.14.1 and its proof; the faithfully flat affine descent step is expanded here

items.strategy: Prove point-injective plus isomorphic residue fields implies universal injectivity. The unramified diagonal is an open immersion and universal injectivity makes it surjective, hence an isomorphism. A flat locally finitely presented map is open; on a principal neighbourhood in its image, the induced affine map is faithfully flat and has multiplication B⊗_A B≅B. Faithful flatness kills B/A, so the map is an isomorphism there.

items.title: Relative normalization and finite-stage descent for quasi-finite maps
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a quasi-finite separated f:X→S with S quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the relative normalization of S in f_*O_X exists with the open X-image required by scheme Zariski Main; étale base change commutes with the construction near finite components, and finite local algebras descend from a suitable finite subalgebra after qcqs gluing.

references.title: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms §§37.22, 37.30, 37.41–44
The Stacks Project, Properties of Schemes, integral algebra finite stages
The Stacks Project, Limits of Schemes, descent of opens and eventual immersion

items.strategy: Let f:X→S be quasi-finite separated with S qcqs. Over each affine U=Spec R in S, the qcqs pushforward lemma identifies M_U=Γ(f^{-1}U,O_X) and its principal localizations, so the integral closures C_U of R inside M_U also localize (clear denominators in monic equations). They glue to an affine-local quasi-coherent algebra C. The published relative-Spec construction gives N=Spec_S C, integral over S, and the evaluation map f′:X→N. For an elementary étale T→S, the qcqs flat-base-change equalizer identifies f_{T,*}O_{X_T} with the pullback of f_*O_X, and the integral-closure étale-base-change lemma identifies N_T with N×_S T. At any x∈X, apply the elementary étale finite-decomposition lemma to split X_T=V⊔W with V finite over T around the selected point. Pushforward and integral closure preserve this product. The integral closure of O_T inside the finite V-algebra is that algebra itself, so N_T=V⊔N_W and f′_T is the identity on V. Thus f′ is an isomorphism over an open neighbourhood of its image point after an étale surjective base change; descent of isomorphisms along this faithfully flat cover gives the same open neighbourhood in N. Repeating at each x shows f′ is an open immersion; because f is quasi-compact, its image J⊂N is quasi-compact. The finite-subalgebra filtration writes C as the filtered union of finite quasi-coherent O_S-subalgebras C_i, so N=lim_i N_i with N_i=Spec_S C_i finite over S and affine transition maps. Cover J by finitely many principal opens on a finite affine cover of S; their defining elements occur at a common index i, yielding a quasi-compact open J_i⊂N_i with inverse image J. Equality of two candidate opens is eventually witnessed by finitely many radical-containment equations, so increasing i makes the descent compatible on overlaps. Since X≅J=lim_i J_i and X is finite type over S, a finite set of affine algebra generators for each X-chart appears in one stage. Hence for some i the map X→J_i is a closed immersion on those charts and globally (the finite-stage closed-immersion lemma); composing with J_i⊂N_i makes X→N_i a quasi-compact immersion. Its scheme-theoretic image T⊂N_i is closed because the ideal ker(O_{N_i}→j_*O_X) is quasi-coherent by the same finite-cover equalizer, and X→T is open: locally the immersion is closed in an open, and the kernel cuts out that closed part. Thus T→S is finite and X→T is a quasi-compact open immersion. AC enters the prime and finite-cover choices and the inherited étale/normalization support.

items.title: Scheme Zariski Main factorization
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If f:X→S is separated and quasi-finite with S quasi-compact and quasi-separated, there is a factorization X→X̄→S with the first map an open immersion and the second finite. For general S this factorization exists Zariski locally on S.

references.title: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms §§37.22, 37.30, 37.41–44

items.strategy: Apply the preceding relative-normalization and finite-stage lemma directly on each qcqs base chart. It constructs the integral relative normalization N, proves the separated quasi-finite X→N is a quasi-compact open immersion using elementary étale finite-component splitting, and then produces a finite S-scheme T as the scheme-theoretic image in a finite subalgebra stage, with X→T open. For qcqs S the construction and finite-stage descent work globally; for arbitrary S, apply it on affine opens and state the resulting factorization only Zariski locally on S. The factorization is full scheme-level Zariski Main, not the published affine algebra statement. AC is inherited from the explicit support lemmas.

items.title: Proper quasi-finite morphisms are finite
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every proper quasi-finite morphism of schemes is finite. For arbitrary base, the assertion is local on the base and uses scheme-level finiteness.

references.title: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms §§37.22, 37.30, 37.41–44
Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37

items.strategy: Locally on the base factor f as X→X̄→S with X→X̄ open and X̄ finite. Since f is proper and X̄ is separated over S, the open map X→X̄ is proper (published proper-source-to-separated-target lemma); hence its image is also closed, and it is an open-and-closed immersion. A closed subscheme of a finite S-scheme is finite by affine quotient, and the local statements glue. This avoids replacing the scheme theorem by the published affine quasi-finite algebra theorem; it depends on the escalated factorization. AC is used for prime/maximal-ideal existence or the cited published algebraic result; no use is made of the incompatible deferred set-theory branch.

items.title: Fibrewise exact finite flat complexes lift over a Noetherian target
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset R$. Let $$0\longrightarrow F_e\longrightarrow F_{e-1}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow F_0$$ be a complex with $e\ge1$, each $F_i$ a finite $S$-module flat over $R$. If its reduction modulo $\mathfrak m$ is exact at every term except possibly $F_0/\mathfrak mF_0$, then the original complex is exact at every term except possibly $F_0$, and $\operatorname{coker}(F_1\to F_0)$ is flat over $R$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.99.5 (tag 00MI), exact complexes and flat cokernels

items.strategy: Induct on the number of arrows. Lift the fibre-injective top arrow to an injection with flat cokernel, quotient the complex by that arrow, and apply the induction hypothesis to the shorter complex.

items.title: A sharp dimension bound makes equations regular on an equidimensional Cohen-Macaulay fibre
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a finite-type $k$-algebra that is Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension $d$. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_i\in A$. If $\dim A/(f_1,\ldots,f_i)\le d-i$, then the tuple is a regular sequence in $A_{\mathfrak q}$ for every prime $\mathfrak q$ containing the $f_j$. When its common zero set is empty the conclusion is vacuous. This is the regularity conclusion of Stacks Lemma 10.129.1.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.129.1 (tag 00R9), dimension bound and regular sequences

items.strategy: extend the equations by quotient parameters at a maximal ideal and use the height theorem to show that the resulting list has the full local dimension.

items.title: A regular sequence lowers dimension exactly in a Cohen-Macaulay local ring
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay local ring of dimension $h$, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_i\in\mathfrak m$ be an $A$-regular sequence. Then $A/(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$ is nonzero and Cohen–Macaulay of dimension $h-i$. In particular $i\le h$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Section 10.129 (tag 00R8), dimension drop in Cohen-Macaulay fibres

items.strategy: prove one-element dimension drop from prime chains and depth, then iterate along the sequence.

items.title: Local fibre dimension equals local ring dimension plus residue transcendence degree
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite-type $k$-algebra, and let $\mathfrak q\in \operatorname{Spec}A$. If $\dim_{\mathfrak q}\operatorname{Spec}A$ means the infimum of the dimensions of open neighbourhoods of $\mathfrak q$, then $$\dim_{\mathfrak q}\operatorname{Spec}A=\dim A_{\mathfrak q}+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak q).$$ This is the affine-point dimension formula used in Stacks Lemma 10.116.3. The formula concerns the local dimension of the fibre scheme, which differs from the dimension of its local ring at a nonclosed point.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.116.3 (tag 00P1), dimension at an affine point

items.strategy: compare each irreducible component through the point with its contribution to the local ring.

items.title: Fibrewise regular sequences persist openly in equidimensional Cohen-Macaulay fibres
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R\to S$ be a finite-type ring map whose fibres $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional of one fixed dimension $d$. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_i\in S$, and put $Z=V(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$. Then the set of $\mathfrak q\in Z$ for which the images of $f_1,\ldots,f_i$ form a regular sequence in the local fibre $S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$, where $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$, is open in $Z$. The empty set $Z$ and empty regular sequence $i=0$ are included.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.129.2 (tag 00RA), openness of regular sequences in fibres

items.strategy: translate regularity at one fibre point into a sharp quotient dimension, spread that bound, and recover regularity on each nearby fibre.

items.title: The highest positive homology of a depth-bounded finite complex has positive depth
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring and $F_\bullet:0\to F_e\to F_{e-1}\to\cdots\to F_0$ a complex of finite $R$-modules with $\operatorname{depth}_R F_j\ge j$ for every $j$. If $i>0$ is the largest index with $H_i(F_\bullet)\ne0$, then $\operatorname{depth}_R H_i(F_\bullet)\ge1$. In particular a nonzero finite-length module cannot be the highest positive homology of such a complex.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.102.8 (tag 00N0), acyclicity lemma

items.strategy: move downward through the exact top of the complex using the depth lemma, then compare boundaries, cycles, and homology at index $i$.

items.title: Reduction of an exact free complex by a nonzerodivisor stays exact above degree one
items.statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring, let $x\in\mathfrak m$ be a nonzerodivisor, and let $F_\bullet:0\to F_e\to F_{e-1}\to\cdots\to F_0$ be a finite complex of finite free $R$-modules. If $H_j(F_\bullet)=0$ for every $j\ge1$, then $H_j(F_\bullet/xF_\bullet)=0$ for every $j\ge2$. Equivalently, the reduced complex is exact at all its terms of degree at least two. The degree-one homology can appear from $x$-torsion in the original cokernel.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.102.7 (tag 00MZ), reduction of exact free complexes

items.strategy: use the homology sequence of multiplication by the nonzerodivisor.

items.title: A unit differential entry splits a contractible two-term summand
items.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $F_\bullet$ a complex of finite free $R$-modules. If one matrix coefficient of $d_i:F_i\to F_{i-1}$ is a unit, then $F_\bullet$ is isomorphic as a complex to the direct sum of a shorter complex and the contractible two-term complex $0\to R\xrightarrow{1}R\to0$ in degrees $i,i-1$. The shorter complex has ranks one smaller in those two degrees and the same ranks elsewhere.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.102.2 (tag 00MT), unit-entry splitting

items.strategy: clear the unit row and column, then use the complex identities to separate adjacent maps.

items.title: Positive-degree exact free complexes split over a depth-zero local ring
items.statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring with a nonzero $a\in R$ annihilated by $\mathfrak m$ (equivalently, $R$ has depth zero). Let $F_\bullet:0\to R^{n_e}\to\cdots\to R^{n_0}$ be a finite free complex exact in every positive degree. Then it is isomorphic to a direct sum of contractible two-term identity complexes and a free module concentrated in degree zero. In particular, with $r_i=n_i-n_{i+1}+\cdots+(-1)^{e-i}n_e$, each differential $d_i$ has rank $r_i$ and its ideal of $r_i$-minors is the unit ideal (with the usual $0$-minor convention).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.102.3 (tag 00MY), depth-zero splitting

items.strategy: find a unit in the highest nonzero differential using the socle element and split pairs until no positive-degree term remains.

items.title: Associated-prime localizations detect elements and have depth zero
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring. The natural map $$R\longrightarrow\prod_{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}(R)}R_{\mathfrak q}$$ is injective. For each $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}(R)$, the local ring $R_{\mathfrak q}$ has a nonzero element annihilated by its maximal ideal $\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak q}$; in particular it has depth zero.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.63.19 (tag 0311), detection at associated localizations
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Section 10.102 (tag 00MR), associated-prime step in the acyclicity criterion

items.strategy: apply associated-prime existence to each nonzero cyclic submodule, then localize its annihilator witness.

items.title: Exact free complexes have the expected ranks and determinantal regular sequences
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $F_\bullet:0\to R^{n_e}\xrightarrow{d_e}\cdots \xrightarrow{d_1}R^{n_0}$ be a finite free complex exact in every positive degree. For $1\le i\le e$ put $r_i=n_i-n_{i+1}+\cdots+(-1)^{e-i}n_e$, and let $I_i$ be the ideal of $r_i$-minors of $d_i$, with the $0$-minor ideal equal to $R$. Then all $(r_i+1)$-minors of $d_i$ vanish, the rank of $d_i$ is exactly $r_i$, and either $I_i=R$ or $I_i$ contains an $R$-regular sequence of length $i$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Proposition 10.102.9 (tag 00N1), necessity direction

items.strategy: detect ranks at associated primes, then induct on complex length after a regular quotient.

items.title: Expected ranks and determinantal regular sequences force a free complex to be exact
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $F_\bullet:0\to R^{n_e}\xrightarrow{d_e}\cdots \xrightarrow{d_1}R^{n_0}$ be a finite free complex. For $1\le i\le e$ put $r_i=n_i-n_{i+1}+\cdots+(-1)^{e-i}n_e$, and let $I_i$ be the ideal of $r_i$-minors of $d_i$, with the $0$-minor ideal equal to $R$. Assume every $r_i$ is nonnegative, all $(r_i+1)$-minors of $d_i$ vanish, and for every $i$, either $I_i=R$ or $I_i$ contains an $R$-regular sequence of length $i$. Then $F_\bullet$ is exact in every positive degree. The assumptions imply each $d_i$ has rank exactly $r_i$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Proposition 10.102.9 (tag 00N1), sufficiency direction

items.strategy: split unit entries, localize the minimal complex and induct on local dimension, then use the depth acyclicity lemma to kill closed-point homology.

items.title: Buchsbaum-Eisenbud rank and grade criterion for exact free complexes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring and $F_\bullet:0\to R^{n_e}\xrightarrow{d_e}\cdots \xrightarrow{d_1}R^{n_0}$ a finite free complex. Define $r_i=n_i-n_{i+1}+\cdots+(-1)^{e-i}n_e$. When $r_i\ge0$, let $I_i$ be the ideal of $r_i$-minors of $d_i$, with the $0$-minor ideal equal to $R$. Then the complex is exact at every positive-degree term if and only if, for all $1\le i\le e$, the integers $r_i$ are nonnegative, all $(r_i+1)$-minors vanish, and either $I_i=R$ or $I_i$ contains an $R$-regular sequence of length $i$. Under these equivalent conditions, $d_i$ has rank exactly $r_i$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Proposition 10.102.9 (tag 00N1), exactness criterion

items.strategy: apply the separately proved necessity and sufficiency directions.

items.title: Fibrewise exactness of a finite free complex is open in a flat Cohen-Macaulay family
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be Noetherian and $R\to S$ a finite-type flat ring map whose nonempty fibres $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional of one fixed dimension $d$. Let $F_\bullet:0\to S^{n_e}\xrightarrow{d_e}\cdots \xrightarrow{d_1}S^{n_0}$ be a finite free complex. For $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ with $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$, reduce the localized complex $F_{\bullet,\mathfrak q}$ modulo $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$. Then the set of points $\mathfrak q$ where this fibre complex is exact in every positive degree is open in $\operatorname{Spec}S$. The case $e=0$ has the whole spectrum as its exactness locus. This is the Stacks 00RB assertion with the equidimensional fibre hypothesis made explicit; it applies in particular to polynomial families.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.129.3 (tag 00RB), openness of fibrewise exactness

items.strategy: lift exactness at the chosen point, fix the expected ranks nearby, and propagate each determinantal regular sequence across nearby fibres.

items.title: Syzygies of a base-flat module over a flat algebra stay base-flat and fibrewise exact
items.statement: Let $R\to P$ be a flat ring map, let $M$ be a $P$-module flat over $R$, and let $$0\to K_n\to F_{n-1}\to\cdots\to F_0\to M\to0$$ be an exact sequence of $P$-modules with $n\ge1$ and each $F_j$ free over $P$. Then every intermediate syzygy, including $K_n$, is flat over $R$. For every ring map $R\to R'$, the sequence obtained by tensoring every term with $R'$ over $R$ is still exact. In particular this holds for a residue field $R'=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and after localizing the result at a prime of $P\otimes_RR'$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Algebra, Theorem 10.129.4 (tag 00RC), flat syzygy and fibre reduction step
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.39.13 (tag 00HM), flatness in exact sequences

items.strategy: move from the quotient $M$ upward through the free resolution, using a tensor diagram to show that each new kernel is flat.

items.title: Open immersions are étale
items.statement: Every open immersion of schemes is étale, including the empty immersion; locally it is Spec A_g→Spec A.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: On a principal chart write A_g as (A[T]/(T−g))_T, for which the derivative is 1. Cover a general open immersion by such charts and use étale locality.

title: Flat Smooth and Etale Morphisms — Examples

items.title: Affine space is smooth
items.statement: For every scheme S and n≥0, A^n_S→S is smooth of pure relative dimension n; its relative differentials have basis dT_1,…,dT_n. The case n=0 is the identity and is étale.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Polynomial algebras are free over the base on monomials. The empty equation list gives a standard-smooth chart, with Ω free on dT_i. Dimension zero gives étale.

items.title: Square-root standard étale chart
items.statement: For a∈A, B=(A[T]/(T²−a))_{2T} is standard étale over A, hence Spec B→Spec A is étale. Over a point where 2a is a unit its fibre is finite étale of degree two; in characteristic two this displayed open chart is empty.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: T²−a is monic and its formal derivative 2T is inverted. Finite freeness before localization follows from the monic relation. On D(2a), T is a unit and 2 is a unit, so the full degree-two algebra is finite étale.

items.title: Flat nodal family fails smoothness
items.statement: Over a field k of characteristic different from 2, the morphism Spec k[x,y,t]/(y²−x²(x+1)−t)→Spec k[t] is flat, but its fibre at t=0 is singular at (x,y)=(0,0), so the morphism is not smooth there.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26
