items.strategy: Eliminate t to identify the total coordinate ring with k[x,y], where k[t] acts by the nonconstant polynomial y²−x²(x+1). This is injective and k[t] is a PID, so the module is torsion-free and flat. On t=0 the two partial derivatives vanish at the origin and the local plane curve has two tangent directions in char≠2.

items.title: The affine line is smooth but not étale
items.statement: A¹_k→Spec k is smooth of relative dimension one but not étale for any field k.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: The relative differential module has basis dT and rank one, whereas an étale morphism has relative dimension zero and vanishing differentials.

items.title: A closed immersion can be unramified without flatness
items.statement: For a field k, Spec(k)→Spec(k[t]) cut out by (t) is unramified and of finite presentation, but not flat and hence not étale.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: The quotient A→A/(t) has Ω_{(A/(t))/A}=0 and residue extension k/k separable, so it is unramified. Tensor the injection (t)↪A with A/(t): its image becomes zero although (t)⊗A/(t)≅k, showing nonflatness.

items.title: Flat finite type need not be open without finite presentation
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let k be a field, R=∏_{n≥1}k and I=⊕_{n≥1}k (finite-support sequences). The quotient map Spec(R/I)→Spec R is flat and finite type, but not open; R/I is not finitely presented as an R-algebra.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Every finitely generated ideal of R is generated by an idempotent, hence R is absolutely flat and R/I is flat. The quotient map has zero algebra generators, so finite type. Its image V(I) is closed. If V(I) were open, its quasi-compact complement and quasi-compactness of V(I) would make it clopen, hence cut out by an idempotent e∈R. Since I is radical, I=(e), contradicting that finite-support sequences form a non-principal ideal. The same nonfinite-generation of I rules out finite presentation of R/I. AC supplies prime ideals for the spectrum and the clopen-idempotent criterion.

items.title: Finite field extensions and étaleness
items.statement: For a finite field extension L/k, Spec L→Spec k is finite étale iff L/k is separable.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Any field extension is flat over k. A finite separable extension has a primitive element with separable minimal polynomial, hence a standard-étale chart. If the map is étale, its residue field extension is finite separable by the published lemma.

items.title: Frobenius on the affine line is finite flat but not smooth
items.statement: For k=F_p, the relative Frobenius F:A¹_k→A¹_k, t↦u^p, is finite free of rank p but not smooth or étale.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: As k[t]-module k[u] has basis 1,u,…,u^{p−1}, using t=u^p. At t=0 the fibre is k[u]/(u^p), nonreduced and therefore not geometrically regular. The relative derivative dt/du=pu^{p−1}=0 corroborates failure of the Jacobian test.

items.title: The family xy=t
items.statement: For any field k, f:Spec k[x,y,t]/(xy−t)→Spec k[t] is flat; its fibre at t=0 is the nodal union of the coordinate axes and f is not smooth at the origin, though it is smooth away from that point.

references.title: Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes §§29.25–29.37
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, 29 August 2022 draft, Chs. 25–26

items.strategy: Eliminate t so the coordinate ring is k[x,y], torsion-free over the PID k[t] because xy is transcendental over k, hence flat. The relative Jacobian row is (y,x); it vanishes precisely at x=y=0, necessarily over t=0. Both coordinates cannot vanish elsewhere, so the other points are smooth.
